→ You design and build production-grade RAG and agentic AI systems end-to-end. From use-case definition through to a working interface in users' hands.
→ Consulting across the Nordics, with clients spanning industries from financial services to manufacturing.
→ You work in cross-functional delivery teams alongside Data Engineers and Platform Engineers, each owning a distinct layer of the stack.
→ Certifications without a debate. Colleagues who are obsessed with the craft. Freedom to grow your way. 


What you'll do
As a GenAI Developer, you own the AI application layer end-to-end: the systems that ingest, retrieve, reason, and respond, plus the lightweight interfaces that put them in front of users. You're the person closest to the end customer. You turn a business problem into a working use-case, from gathering requirements and aligning stakeholders to shipping a production system people actually use.
You come in before the solution is defined. Together with the client, you shape what gets built, then you build it. You work alongside Data Engineers and Platform Engineers, each owning a distinct layer of the stack. Your layer is where the model meets the business problem, and where the user meets the product.
A few examples of what this looks like in practice:
A production RAG system for a financial services client, letting internal teams navigate regulatory documentation using generative AI. From ingestion through to answer generation, quality evaluation, and a lightweight front-end for day-to-day use.



An agentic AI solution in the FinOps space, applying LLM reasoning over infrastructure data to drive cloud cost optimization beyond what rule-based tooling can handle.



AI capability building at enterprise clients: use-case workshops, requirements definition, and architecture advisory on agents and coding tools for senior technical audiences.

The bar for what "done" means here is high: production-grade, observable, secure and used.


What you get
Assignments that accelerate you. Every 6–18 months you're in a new engagement. New industry, new architecture decisions, new stakeholders to earn trust from. You'll face more distinct technical challenges in two years here than most engineers see in five.
Work that's hard to come by elsewhere. Agentic AI in enterprise environments is one of the most technically demanding spaces in the industry right now. The problems here aren't solved yet, and you'll be among the people solving them.
Your direction, your call. Want to go deep technically and become the go-to person for enterprise AI architecture? Go for it. Want to lead client engagements, own stakeholder relationships and drive use-cases from discovery to production? Also go for it. Both paths are real and equally valued.
People who make you better. The people here are genuinely passionate about technology, not as a job, but as something they care about. Engineers who go deep because they want to, follow the space obsessively, and get restless when things stop moving. That's what keeps Redeploy consistently ahead, and it's what you'll feel from day one.
The perks. 30 days vacation · hybrid work and flexible hours · private medical insurance · pension (ITP1) · wellness allowance 5,000 SEK · free choice of tools and tech · free breakfast, soda and snacks · yearly gatherings and AW's · a team with genuine interests outside work — gaming, food, running, padel, golf, football, cycling.


Who you are
You care whether your AI systems actually work, not just whether they run, and you have an instinct for finding failure modes before they reach production. You care about how users interact with it, and you don't consider a use-case done until it's working end-to-end, interface included.
You might come from a fullstack engineering or traditional ML/Data background. What matters is that you're already building AI solutions, whether that's a side project, a POC, or a deep dive into a new framework. Curiosity is a given. The question is whether you act on it.
You like being close to the people who'll use what you build. You can run a requirements workshop, figure out what a stakeholder actually needs versus what they asked for, and explain why a retrieval pipeline is underperforming, all with the same clarity.


What you bring
Strong requirements engineering and stakeholder management skills, you can drive a use-case from problem definition to delivery, keeping technical and non-technical audiences aligned throughout



Strong Python skills and solid software engineering fundamentals: clean code, testing, version control, system design



Production experience with RAG architectures: chunking strategies, embedding models, vector search, hybrid retrieval, reranking, and retrieval evaluation



Hands-on experience with agentic frameworks such as LangChain, LlamaIndex, AutoGen, or CrewAI, including tool use, memory management, and multi-agent orchestration



Experience with Azure AI Services or Azure OpenAI, including integration across Azure services in production environments



Ability to build lightweight front-end interfaces for AI applications to make prototypes and internal tools usable beyond the terminal



Strong plus: multi-agent architecture design, front-end development skills (React, Streamlit, or similar), containerization and MLOps awareness, experience in regulated industries, Azure AI-102 certification, prior consulting experience, Swedish language skills.


About Redeploy
Redeploy is where cloud, data, and AI come together in production. We help Nordic enterprises design, build, and operate modern tech platforms and AI solutions that are secure, scalable, and production-ready. Engineers at heart, we work hands-on across Azure, AWS, and Databricks from strategy to operations.

About Antrino
Antrino Labs is building the platform that makes every square meter intelligent.
The physical world runs on processes nobody can actually see. Goods move, machines idle, space goes unused, and decisions about all of it are based on samples, guesses, and reports written after the fact. Antrino lets any organization deploy vision intelligence into a physical space and get back what is actually happening there, as structured, real-time information it can act on. Not a research project or a custom integration, but a platform where you describe what matters and deploy it.
We have grown from 6 people to a team of 28 in less than a year, closed our Seed round, announced together with Dagens Industri, and are registered with Inspektionen för strategiska produkter (ISP), the Swedish authority for strategic and dual-use products. Everything we build follows Privacy by Design.
The role
You will build the services that turn a customer's intent into working intelligence.
When a customer builds something in Studio, our composition canvas, that graph has to become a running system: a plan that decides which models to call, in what order, gated by cost and confidence, and that produces events and evidence a customer can trust. You will work on the compiler that turns the graph into an execution plan, the runtime that executes it, and the Python and TypeScript services that detection, classification, and measurement run through.
You will also work on our Agent, which interviews customers, proposes and edits these graphs, and deploys them with confirmation. Getting an LLM to reliably manipulate a structured graph, validate it, and explain its reasoning is a real engineering problem, not a prompting exercise.
The role sits between the team building our first-party detection models and the engineers building the product interface. It is backend systems engineering for a product whose core logic is built out of AI calls.
What you will work on
Backend services for detection, classification, and measurement, largely in Python with FastAPI
The compiler that turns a Studio graph into an execution plan, and the runtime that deploys and runs it
Routing logic that decides which model handles which work, including cost gating where a cheap model decides when an expensive one runs
The Agent's interview, graph-editing, and deployment flows that turn natural language into a working pipeline
Integrating our first-party detection models, and frontier model APIs where they do something ours do not yet, behind one clean interface
Turning raw model output into structured, auditable events and evidence an operator can trust
APIs and data models for streams, behaviors, runs, and events in PostgreSQL with row-level security
Tests and evaluation harnesses for logic that includes non-deterministic model calls
Debugging production issues that span a customer request, our orchestration, and the model call underneath



Our stack
You do not need experience with all of this, but you should recognize most of it and be able to argue about it.
Backend: Python, FastAPI, TypeScript, Node.jsData: PostgreSQL through Supabase, with row-level security, 
Streaming: RTSP ingestion, RTSP→HLS conversion, live and archive pipelines
Infrastructure: Azure, GitHub Actions, on-site compute reached over Tailscale
Who we are looking for Substantial backend experience on production systems, ideally where an LLM or ML model was part of the core logic rather than a bolted-on feature
Strong Python, and comfort in TypeScript or Node.js
Real experience designing APIs, data models, and service boundaries, including PostgreSQL
Experience building with LLM APIs beyond a chat wrapper: tool use, structured output, agentic flows, or a model as one step in a larger pipeline
An understanding of how to test systems with non-deterministic components
Experience with real-time or streaming data is a strong advantage
Excellent written and spoken English. Swedish is a plus, not a requirement



You can reason about a graph or compiler-shaped problem even if you have never built a compiler. You make decisions with incomplete information, take responsibility for the outcome, and say so clearly when something you built was wrong.
Life at Antrino

When Anyfin goes down, someone’s loan payment doesn’t go through. Make sure it doesn’t.
You open your laptop on Monday and find out the primary database failed at 3am on Sunday. Services reconnected in seconds and no customer noticed a thing. We’d practised exactly that failover the week before.
If that’s your idea of a good weekend, we should talk.
The foundation is built. Now it needs to scale.
Anyfin helps people refinance expensive consumer credit on better terms. Since 2017 we’ve helped people across Sweden, Finland and Germany take back control of their finances. We’re profitable, we have a banking licence that lets us operate across the EU, and we’re getting ready to launch new products and enter new markets. Our ambition is to be a pan-European company by 2030.
Every one of those steps puts more weight on our platform: more traffic, more integrations, more markets and more regulators who expect us to prove that we’re resilient, not just say it.
The team is small and intentionally so. We’d rather grow what each engineer can do than how many engineers we have.
The actual job
You’ll own reliability across the platform. That covers how our services run on Kubernetes and GCP, how we deploy, how we scale and how we recover when something breaks. You’ll decide what “reliable enough” means for each part of the system and make it measurable.
You’ll make problems visible before customers feel them. That means monitoring, alerting and logging that tell us what’s wrong and why, not dashboards nobody opens. When an alert fires, it should matter.
You’ll make incidents boring. You’ll shape how we respond, who gets paged, how we communicate and how we learn. That means blameless reviews that lead to real changes, not just documents.
You’ll build the paved road. Engineers should be able to ship safely and quickly without thinking about infrastructure every time. You’ll work on CI/CD, infrastructure as code and the tooling that makes the right way the easy way.
You’ll help us meet the bar a bank is held to. As a regulated lender, operational resilience isn’t optional. You’ll help us turn requirements like DORA into systems and practices that actually work, not just policies we can point to.
You’ll keep an eye on cost. Scaling into new markets shouldn’t mean scaling our cloud bill at the same rate.
Reliability in an AI-native company
AI isn’t a side tool here. It’s built into how we work across engineering, analytics, operations and product, and our tech team has built an AI-connected data and code environment on frontier models.
That shows up in reliability work too. AI can help read logs, trace incidents and draft runbooks faster than any of us. It also means more systems in production act on data without questioning it, and more automation can change things on its own.
Part of this role is working out what reliability means in that world: where AI makes us faster, where it needs guardrails, and how we make sure we’re never the last to know when something goes wrong.
The people
You’ll work closely with backend engineers, data engineers, product teams and our engineering managers, who care a lot about getting things right. Sometimes a little too much. Propose a new alert and someone will ask how many times it would have fired last month. We prefer it that way.
They’re also generous with what they know, quick to laugh and happy to change their minds when you make a better case. As long as you can back it up.
This sounds like you if…
You have solid experience in SRE, platform or infrastructure engineering, ideally in a product company where reliability directly affects customers. You’ve run production workloads on Kubernetes in a cloud environment and are comfortable with infrastructure as code.
You write real code, not just YAML. Our main stack is TypeScript, Node.js, Python and Go, running on Kubernetes and GCP. Experience with GCP and Terraform is a plus, but you don’t need to know every technology in our stack. You’re comfortable reading, debugging and improving services, and the judgment you bring matters more than ticking every box.
You’ve built observability that people actually use, and you’ve been on call for systems that mattered. You know the difference between an alert and noise.
You’re pragmatic. You care about reliability, but you know 100% uptime isn’t the goal and that over-engineering has a cost too. You can explain that trade-off to engineers and non-engineers alike.
Experience from fintech, banking or another regulated environment is a plus, but not a requirement.
More than anything, you can tell us about a system you made more reliable. Not just what you changed, but what it made possible for the team and the business.
A few practical notes
This role is based at our office on Drottninggatan 92 in Stockholm, and we work from the office. We think great teams and culture are built when people meet in person, especially at this stage.
EU work authorisation is required.
If you’d rather prevent the next incident than write the postmortem for it, we’d love to hear from you.

About Epiminds
We’re building Lucy, an AI system that investigates marketing performance and carries approved changes through to execution.
Behind that work is a backend coordinating model calls, external APIs, persistent state, and code running in sandboxes. We’re a small team in Stockholm building the infrastructure this product needs.


The Problem
Agent workloads are difficult to predict. One request can become several parallel investigations. A task can pause for approval and continue later. A worker can disappear after an external API accepts a change but before the result is saved.
Retrying may duplicate the action. Giving up may leave the work unfinished. Keeping everything ready reduces latency but consumes idle compute.
The system has to know what happened, who owns the next step, and what is safe to repeat—while keeping data isolated and costs under control.


The Role
You’ll own the execution infrastructure, data systems, and reliability behind Lucy.
You’ll work across application code, databases, and cloud infrastructure, taking changes from design through deployment and operation. Your decisions will shape how the product handles more work and recovers when things fail.


What You’ll Do
Make execution durable. Build scheduling, queues, leases, cancellation, and recovery for work that outlives an individual request.
Make retries safe. Preserve execution state and prevent duplicate events from repeating external actions.
Run agent compute efficiently. Improve sandbox startup, worker scaling, resource limits, and cleanup.
Build dependable data flows. Handle pagination, partial failures, changing provider contracts, and datasets that should be streamed rather than held in memory.
Make failures explainable. Connect traces, logs, and cost data so the team can find bottlenecks and resolve incidents.

What We’re Looking For
You’ve operated backend systems in production and owned their reliability. You understand database design, distributed state, queues, and the difference between a failed request and a failed operation.
You’re comfortable with containers and cloud infrastructure. You can explain what breaks under load, how recovery works, and when a simpler design is enough.
Our stack includes TypeScript, Node.js, Supabase/PostgreSQL, Redis, Temporal, Cloud Run, GKE, Modal, Docker, and Pulumi.


Why Join Now
Execution is central to the product. You’ll shape how agents run, how their work survives failures, and how infrastructure cost changes as usage grows.


What we offer
Competitive salary and meaningful equity.
Healthcare, retirement savings, and wellbeing support.
Office catering.

Hiring process
Recruiter screening.
Technical task.
Code interview.
Trial with us in the office.

We welcome applicants of all backgrounds.

Company Description

Vattenfall is a leading European energy company serving approximately 12 million customers and employing around 21,000 people. We believe there is a way to build a future where everyone can choose fossil-free ways to move, make, and live.

Job Description

Are you a student looking to apply your knowledge to real-world solutions that support the energy transition? With us, you will have the opportunity to complete your thesis project close to the business, working alongside experienced specialists and tackling challenges where your ideas and perspectives can make a real difference.
About the Thesis Work
The Thesis will be held under Corporate Security & Resilience function at Vattenfall which is a modern, flexible, and agile unit that is operating in a challenging and rapidly changing environment. We strive to embed security & resilience into all our business operations and we apply a holistic and risk-based approach to constantly adopt and improve our security posture.
Background and Scope
Cybersecurity exercises, including tabletop exercises and functional exercises are an important part of organizational resilience, particularly for critical infrastructure operators where information technology (IT) and operational technology (OT) environments are interconnected. The effectiveness of such exercises depends on the realism, technical accuracy, and relevance of the scenario and its supporting injects (alerts, emails, media reports, decision points).
However, developing scenarios and injects is often manual and resource intensive activity. Exercise planners must translate and combine multiple variables into a sequence that is credible for both IT and OT participants. Generative AI and large language models can support on scenario development, structured content generation and role-based dialogues, while agentic capabilities can enable more adaptive exercises by proposing subsequent injects.
The thesis will investigate how generative AI can support both the design and adaptive facilitation of IT/OT cybersecurity exercises. The thesis will follow a qualitative approach, focusing on the development of a conceptual framework and workflow specification for AI assisted exercise design. The proposed framework and workflow will be evaluated through expert review and walkthroughs with focus on real world applicability and relevance for IT/OT cybersecurity environments.
The thesis is expected to deliver: 
An academic framework for generative AI assisted scenarios and injection design;
A small library of reviewed example artifacts demonstrating the framework;
A documented workflow covering source preparation, scenario generation, state tracking, adaptive inject selection, human approval and debrief support.
A limited demonstrator or simulation showing how participant decisions can change subsequent injects and scenario outcomes.
Output and summary of experts after review where they will analyze the risk factors and the possible adoption issue that they foresee.

This thesis project is for 2 students.

Qualifications

We are looking for students who are about to complete their academic studies and are eager to apply their knowledge in a real-world setting through a thesis project at Vattenfall. You are someone who shares our values and identifies with our principles: Active, Open, Positive and Safety.
Furthermore, we see that you have: 
Education - Computer Science, Software Engineering
Fluency in written and spoken English as the thesis project will be in English

Scope: 30 credits (M.Sc Level)

Location: Göteborg or Stockholm

Application deadline: 2026-11-18
